## Appearance

Rosemary West is a tall, fair, and placid woman with a finely shaped face, pink cheeks, and a high white forehead. She has large, calm, blue eyes that carry a friendly expression alongside a slow, sweet smile. Her golden head features hair of a warm, molasses taffy color, which is worn pinned over her head in sleek, close coils.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P7](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0007), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. ## History

At seventeen, Rosemary West was engaged to a young sailor who subsequently drowned, and following her mother's death, she made a solemn vow with her sister [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) never to marry. Years later, [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) met her by a spring in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) and walked her home, sparking rumors of a romance. After comforting Mr. Meredith's daughter [Faith](../character/faith.md) over a lost pet, Rosemary was unexpectedly proposed to by Mr. Meredith; realizing she loved him, she asked for time to consider, but [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) fiercely refused to release her from her vow, forcing Rosemary to send him a cold rejection. Later, after [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) asked Rosemary to release [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) from her vow so they could wed, Rosemary agreed, but [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) ultimately refused to marry Norman if it meant leaving Rosemary to live alone. Finally, Mr. Meredith's daughter [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) visited Rosemary to ask her to marry her father, prompting Rosemary to give [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) a note for him that restored his spirits.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P5](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. ## Quotes

> "It is such a help to talk things over. I know. I don’t suppose I can be as good at understanding as Mrs. Blythe—but I promise you that I won’t laugh."
>
> — Rosemary West — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P14](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0014)

> "But I would have been just as naughty, Faith—I wouldn’t have told him they were scorching—and I don’t believe I would ever have been a bit sorry for my wickedness, either."
>
> — Rosemary West — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P28](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0028)

> "Dearest, if a minister doesn’t behave as a gentleman we are not bound to respect his coat-tails. I know I would just have loved to see Jimmy Perry’s coat-tails burning up. It must have been fun."
>
> — Rosemary West — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P30](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0030)

> "If you hang the cage far enough from the wall I don’t think the cat could harm it. I’ll tell you just how to take care of it and I’ll bring it to Ingleside for you the next time I come down."
>
> — Rosemary West — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P35](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0035)

> "You made it so knackily. I never saw anyone make a birch cup so since my little brother used to make them long ago—before he died."
>
> — Rosemary West — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P15](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0015)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--rosemary-west.md)

[Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) considers Rosemary to be a delightful friend and a kindred spirit of the race of [Joseph](../character/joseph.md). The two share mutual acquaintances in the community, with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) following local gossip regarding Rosemary's potential romance with the minister.

### [Ellen West](../character/ellen-west.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/ellen-west--rosemary-west.md)

[Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) is Rosemary's sister, with whom she made a solemn vow ten years prior never to marry so they could live together. When [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) proposes, Rosemary begs [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) to release her from this promise, but [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) fiercely refuses to do so. This forces Rosemary to send a heartbreaking refusal to John while [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) attempts to rationalize her harsh decision.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050), [v5 CHAPTER XII. AN EXPLANATION AND A DARE P5](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0005), +22 more_

### [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/john-meredith--rosemary-west.md)

[John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) falls deeply in love with Rosemary and considers her the only woman for him. Though their easy, pleasant interactions lead to his marriage proposal, their romance ends in heartbreak because Rosemary is bound by a prior promise to her sister that prevents her from accepting him.
